name: Ferrochem ChemGuard Pressline Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty elbow-length gauntlets in matte acid-yellow nitrile over a woven aramid liner, heat-stamped with Ferrochem's black triangle hazard marks along the cuff. The palms are triple-laminated; the fingertips reinforced with ribbed grip ridges worn smooth on older pairs. Color fades from handling — veterans' gloves run pale gold at the fingers, vivid at the wrist.

Standard issue on Ferrochem processing floors and widely adopted across Tier 1-2 chemical handling jobs. the Gray Zone workers scavenge them from disposal bins; the real ones resist acids that eat substitutes in minutes.
functionality: Rated for Class-IV acid splash, moderate heat (up to 180°C contact), and puncture resistance. Extended cuff seals against sleeve openings. Not aug-compatible — chrome hands cannot wear these; intended for unaugmented workers or those with basic wrist-port augments only.
what_it_says: You work with materials that eat through lesser gear, and you cannot afford to stop.
worn_by: the Gray Zone scavengers handling reclaimed industrial waste
story_hooks: A pair found in a the Gray Zone drain tunnel still has a wrist-tag with a worker ID — the worker is listed as missing on Ferrochem's internal incident log.
Knockoff versions circulate the Gray Zone market, indistinguishable until the acid hits — someone is deliberately flooding the market with fakes.
A Tier 3 lab inspector wears a pair under formal sleeves during a facility audit, suggesting they know something about today's inspection that the workers don't.

physical_description.visual_profile: Industrial-grade elbow-length gauntlets with a distinctly utilitarian silhouette. The matte acid-yellow dominates, creating high visibility on processing floors. Sharp black hazard triangles march down the cuff in rigid rows—unmistakably corporate issue. The form is slightly bulky at the wrist, tapering toward reinforced fingertips.
physical_description.fit: Snug compression fit through the palm and fingers, looser at the forearm to allow layering over work clothes. The cuff sits high on the wrist with slight overlap for seal integrity.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte nitrile outer shell over woven aramid liner—chemically resistant and heat-treated for durability.
physical_description.texture: Smooth matte finish on the outer nitrile; the palms feature triple-laminated ribbed grip ridges that wear smooth with heavy use. The cuff interior is slightly tacky from heat-stamping process.
physical_description.color_scheme: Vivid acid-yellow primary with matte black heat-stamped hazard triangles in a repeating pattern along both cuffs. Wear patterns create two-tone fading—pale gold at fingertips and palm centers, vibrant yellow at wrists and outer forearms.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit wrist opening with an optional elastic retention strap; no zippers or snaps—designed for quick donning/removal.
distinctive_features: Black heat-stamped Ferrochem hazard triangle marks—corporate branding and chemical warning symbol combined
Triple-laminated reinforced palms for acid resistance
Ribbed grip ridges on fingertips (smooth on veteran pairs from friction)
Visible wear patterns showing two-tone color fade—pale gold at stress points
Elbow-length coverage for full forearm protection
Slightly stiffened cuff structure for seal integrity on chemical processing equipment
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate-issued PPE; expensive enough that Tier 5 workers actively scavenge them from disposal bins.
physical_description.cultural_context: Ferrochem processing floor worker, chemical handler, industrial safety compliance. Wearing these signals corporate affiliation or serious chemical handling credentials. Scavenged pairs signal resourcefulness and understanding of what actually works versus cheap knockoffs.
physical_description.condition_typical: Newer pairs: pristine matte finish, vivid yellow, sharp black marks. Veteran pairs: faded two-tone coloring, smooth worn grip ridges, slight discoloration from chemical contact, minor creasing at flex points.
